title: CC Plugin Manifest
description: Registration document for a plugin container, analogous to an AWS Batch job definition. Field names from cc-home/docs/05_plugin-manifest.md. Registered once per plugin and referenced by name:revision from compute manifests, so every field here is frozen against already-deployed DAGs.

name.description: Registered plugin name. The compute provider's identifier for the plugin.

image_and_tag.x-cc-rule: STD-OPS-001: ':latest' MUST NOT appear in a registered manifest. A massively parallel run must be pinned to something reproducible. Prefer shipping a digest alongside the tag.

command.description: Command parameter array. When omitted the image's CMD/ENTRYPOINT is used.
command.x-cc-rule: STD-WIRE-023: SHOULD be explicit rather than inherited, so registered behavior is inspectable and troubleshooting does not require rebuilding an image to learn what ran. Supports AWS Batch Ref:: parameter substitution, resolved against the compute manifest's inputs.parameters.

vcpu.description: CPU units. Documented sample uses a STRING ('"2"'), so both string and number must parse. This is why the type is a union and not a number: tightening it would reject registered manifests.

extraHosts.description: Extra host mappings, e.g. 'host.docker.internal:host-gateway'. Used for local Docker compute.

compute_environment.x-cc-known-divergence: extraHosts is camelCase while its siblings are lowercase single words and its parent is snake_case. Frozen by STD-WIRE-005 and listed in standards.md Appendix C. The casing is inconsistent WITHIN one object, which makes it the most likely target of an accidental 'tidy up' refactor.
compute_environment.x-cc-rule: STD-PLG-030: vcpu and memory MUST be measured from a representative run with stated headroom, not guessed. Under-declared memory is OOM-kill roulette across a fleet; over-declared is the dominant cost driver in FFRD batch runs.

environment.description: Environment variables injected into the running container.

credentials.description: Values mapped from the compute provider's secret store into the container environment.

value.description: A secretsmanager reference, never a literal.

items.x-cc-rule: STD-SEC-010 / STD-DATA-004: a literal credential here is a merge blocker. Documented form is 'secretsmanager:NAME::'. Note the value pattern permits the trailing empty segments the docs show.

execution_timeout.description: Seconds. null or absent means no timeout.
execution_timeout.x-cc-known-divergence: The plugin manifest calls this execution_timeout; the COMPUTE MANIFEST calls the equivalent override job_timeout. Two names, one concept, both live. Frozen.

privileged.x-cc-rule: STD-PLG-031 / STD-SEC-012: setting true grants nearly host-equivalent access. Requires an ADR plus a named device in linux_parameters.devices.

host_path.description: Device path on the host, e.g. /dev/fuse.

nameValue.x-cc-note: Array-of-pairs rather than an object, so ordering is preserved and the same shape serves environment and credentials. Values are strings even when numeric ('"42"', '"NO"', '"FALSE"'); SDKs MUST NOT coerce types here.
